<section class="hero" aria-label="Introduction">
  <div class="hero-photo">
    <img src="assets/img/profile.jpg" alt="Portrait of Matej Opatrny" width="600" height="800" fetchpriority="high">

  <div class="hero-text">
    <span class="eyebrow">Economist · Charles University, Prague</span>
    <h1>Matej Opatrny <span class="titles">MSc, PhD</span></h1>
    <p class="bio">
      Matej Opatrny is an economist at the Institute of Economic Studies, Faculty of Social Sciences,
      Charles University, Prague, and a researcher at the Charles University Environment Centre.
      His research spans microeconomics, environmental economics, agricultural policy evaluation and
      microsimulation modelling, with a focus on the distributional effects of climate and fiscal
      policy on households. His household microsimulation work provides analytical support to the
      Czech Ministry of the Environment and the Ministry of Agriculture. Outside academia, he has
      worked at McKinsey &amp; Company and as an economic analyst at Expobank.
    </p>
    <p class="bio">
      He also knows agricultural policy from the other side of the fence. Together with his parents,
      his brother and sister-in-law, he runs a small family farm of around 20 hectares in Šumava,
      where the cows are his own and looking after them is his job. He is married and has two
      children.
    </p>
